NOTE: Anker 633 Magnetic Battery (A1641): Can charge most phones up to three times with a combined output of 18W (MagSafe wireless charging, USB-C PD, USB-A port). Features strong internal magnets and a fold-out stand. Kickstand is a bit flimsy. Prices observed at $40 (Amazon) and $42 (Walmart). [hands-on][expert-domain] (Source 1)
NOTE: Satechi Duo Wireless Charger Power Stand: Can output up to 20W and fully charge most phones up to three times. Can wirelessly charge two devices simultaneously. It's hefty and lacks magnets, but has a super sturdy phone stand. Prices observed at $100, $60 (Satechi with code CPTS14), $70 (Amazon), and $100 (Walmart). [hands-on][expert-domain] (Source 1)
NOTE: Anker MagGo Power Bank (10K, Slim): Has a 10,000 mAh capacity, 15W total wattage, 1 USB-C port (input and output). Weighs 7oz (200g). Measured to provide 1.8 charges for a 5,000 mAh device. Features fast charging in a slim design and strong magnetic grip. It is heavier than expected and on the pricey side. [hands-on][expert-domain] (Source 2)
NOTE: Anker 10,000mAh Portable Charger (with integrated cable): Has a 10,000 mAh battery capacity. Features an integrated woven USB-C cable, an additional USB-C port, a USB-A port, and a front-facing display for remaining charge. Described as relatively compact and pocketable. Observed sale price of $22.99, down from $29.99. [hands-on][expert-domain] (Source 3)
NOTE: Anker PowerCore 10K: Has a 10,000mAh capacity. Features one micro USB port for input, one USB-C port (input and output), and one USB-A port (output). Can charge two devices at once. Anker claims it can charge an iPhone 15 twice, a Galaxy S23 up to 1.93 times, and an iPad mini 6 up to 1.23 times. Not explicitly reviewed by TechRadar, but the brand is recommended. Observed sale price of $19.99, down from $25.99. [expert-domain] (Source 4)

A.summary: For iPhone users in 2026, Qi2-certified magnetic banks are the clear winners. Hands-on testing by Engadget and Wirecutter confirms Anker's MagGo 10K and 633 models charge fastest and most reliably, while Anker's wired 10K models remain the best budget pocketable options.

products.name: Anker MagGo Power Bank (10K) - Qi2 Certified
pros: Most well-rounded MagSafe battery tested by Engadget hands-on
One of first Qi2-certified products - faster than previous gen Anker 633
LCD display shows remaining percentage and time to full/empty
Measured 1.64 full iPhone 15 charges and 45 min to 50% in hands-on testing
Includes USB-C to USB-C cable and USB-C PD in/out
cons: Weighs 8.82 oz and 4.22 x 2.71 x 0.78 inches - bulkier than 5K options
Self-recharge still takes 2h 26m for 4-100% per measured results
products.verdict: Engadget hands-on testing confirms this is the top all-around pick for iPhone in 2026. Qi2 gives you true 15W magnetic charging, the display is genuinely useful, and measured 1.64 iPhone 15 charges beats marketing claims. It's the one we'd buy.

products.name: Anker 633 Magnetic Battery (A1641)
pros: Recommended as best wireless power bank by Wirecutter hands-on testing
Strong internal magnets and fold-out stand for desk viewing
Combined output 18W with MagSafe wireless, USB-C PD, and USB-A
Can charge most phones up to three times per manufacturer claim
cons: Kickstand is a bit flimsy per hands-on testing
Not Qi2-certified, so slower than newer MagGo 10K generation
Wireless charging can be finicky compared to wired

specs.features: MagSafe wireless, USB-C PD, USB-A, fold-out stand

products.verdict: Wirecutter hands-on testing found this comes closest to nailing wireless on-the-go charging. If you want a proven magnetic bank with a stand and extra USB-A port and don't need Qi2, this $40 pick is still excellent, despite the flimsy kickstand.

products.name: Anker MagGo Power Bank (10K, Slim)
pros: TechRadar top pick for all-around power bank per expert-domain review
Fast charging in a slim design with strong magnetic grip
10,000 mAh capacity with 15W total wattage
Measured to provide 1.8 charges for a 5,000 mAh device
cons: Heavier than expected at 7oz (200g) per hands-on testing
On the pricey side compared to wired 10K banks
products.verdict: TechRadar hands-on testing calls this the slim magnetic sweet spot. You get the same 10K capacity as the standard MagGo but in a more pocketable chassis, though weight is still noticeable. Good if you prioritize thinness over display features.

products.name: Anker 10,000mAh Portable Charger with Integrated Cable
pros: Integrated woven USB-C cable - no extra cable to carry
Additional USB-C port plus USB-A port for two-device charging
Front-facing display for remaining charge
Relatively compact and pocketable per hands-on testing
cons: No magnetic wireless charging - wired only
products.verdict: Hands-on testing by TechRadar highlights this as the practical budget pick for iPhone when you don't need MagSafe. The built-in cable solves the most common travel annoyance, and at $22.99 it's half the price of magnetic models while still fast-charging via USB-C PD.

products.name: Anker PowerCore 10K
pros: Can charge two devices at once
Considered one of slimmest and lightest 10,000mAh chargers on paper
Anker claims 2x iPhone 15 charges, 1.93x Galaxy S23, 1.23x iPad mini 6
Lowest price in roundup at $19.99 sale
cons: Uses micro USB for input - outdated vs USB-C only
Not explicitly reviewed by TechRadar hands-on, brand recommendation only

specs.ports: 1x micro USB input, 1x USB-C input/output, 1x USB-A output

products.verdict: Expert-domain coverage from TechRadar recommends the brand but notes this specific model hasn't had a dedicated hands-on review. Still, at $19.99 it's the cheapest credible 10K bank from an established brand, and dual-output is useful if you can live with micro-USB input.

products.name: Satechi Duo Wireless Charger Power Stand
pros: Can wirelessly charge two devices simultaneously
Super sturdy phone stand per hands-on testing
Up to 20W output and up to three full phone charges
Works as both power bank and desk stand
cons: Hefty and lacks magnets per hands-on testing - phone can slide
Expensive at $100 MSRP, even $60-$70 sale is high
products.verdict: Wirecutter hands-on testing recommends this only for dual-device desk use. The lack of magnets is a dealbreaker for on-the-go iPhone charging, and heft makes it a poor portable pick, but if you need to wirelessly charge two devices at once on a nightstand, it's uniquely capable.
